creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen in 0.24.0 with two windows open. Window A's Needs you strip showed two cards titled by bare pane ids (`p2jg064x2x  Done 1m`, `p2jg0jmmx9  Done <1m`). Both panes were named agents with callsigns (prairie, leopard), but they lived in window B's tabs.

The core's asking list (`Session::asking_entries` in crates/muster-seam/src/session.rs) is built from attention across every backend, not per window, so each window's strip gets every window's askers. `NeedsYouModel.cards` (Sources/MusterMac/NeedsYou.swift) takes the title from the window's own roster, and a pane the roster does not hold falls back to `entry.pane`, with no chord keys. The fallback was meant for a pane the shell has not caught up on (fd462515); a pane held by another window hits it on every render.

The callsign is already known to the core for those panes: `muster window --json` from window A lists them, with callsign and name, under `other_windows`. Either carry the callsign (and label) in AskingEntry so the shell never needs its roster for the title, or decide that a window's strip lists only its own askers and drop the others. The first keeps the strip in agreement with `focus --asking`, which the model's doc comment says it must.
title: Needs you names another window's agents by pane id
